svg.text: Spin coater UV lid: argon diffuser, concept (issue #251)
substrate (up to about Ø220), wet film on top
out over the edge to the lid gaps
Ø60 flange
Ø44 body
gap 15 (assumed)
SECTION THROUGH THE AXIS (scale 2:1)
VIEW FROM BELOW (scale 1.5:1)
52 holes Ø1 on a 4 mm hex pitch inside Ø30
dashed: flange, plenum, baffle and posts (hidden)
CALLOUTS
1 PTFE tube 4 x 2, argon in
2 PC4-M10 push-in fitting (M10 x 1; check the fitting)
3 M10 x 1 tapped 6 deep, Ø2.5 inlet to the plenum
4 Cup, ASA by FFF, printed boss up; plenum Ø34 x 6
5 Baffle Ø14 on 3 posts Ø2, 1.0 below the roof
6 3 x M2 countersunk: the face plate comes off for cleaning
7 Face plate, ASA, Ø1 holes drilled after printing
8 3 x M3 on Ø52, nuts under the LED plate
9 LED plate, acrylic t 3 (assumed), centre hole opened to Ø45
NOTES
1. Concept sketch, not a shop drawing. Assumed until measured: LED plate thickness, the lid-to-substrate gap,
the LED ring (keep the puck nearly flush so it shades no LED) and the push-in fitting's thread.
2. Two ASA parts by FFF: the cup boss up, with support under the flange (8 mm overhang); the plenum roof bridges Ø34,
where sag is harmless. The face plate prints flat with its posts and baffle.
ASA is UV stable next to the 365 to 405 nm LEDs. Clean with IPA: acetone dissolves ASA.
3. The baffle turns the inlet jet before the face, so the holes in line with the inlet do not take most of the flow.
4. At 2 L/min: inlet 6.8 m/s, each hole 0.8 m/s, mean over the hole field 47 mm/s;
hole drop about 2 Pa against 0.5 Pa dynamic pressure at the baffle exit.
5. At 5 L/min: inlet 17.0 m/s, each hole 2.0 m/s, mean over the hole field 118 mm/s;
hole drop about 10 Pa against 3.0 Pa dynamic pressure at the baffle exit.
6. If the face flows unevenly on the bench, lay a fine stainless mesh on the face plate inside the plenum.
7. Argon 1.66 kg/m^3 (20 C, 1 atm); hole discharge coefficient 0.6 assumed.
